newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Siemens' Osram sees profit static.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Siemens' Osram sees profit static.

text.p: Osram GmbH, the lighting unit of Germany's Siemens AG, said on Tuesday write-offs in its U.S. unit and falling prices were expected to prevent profit from rising next year.
But profit growth should resume after the 1996-97 business year, as new markets lift sales to about seven 7 billion marks ($4.5 billion) by the year 2000, Osram predicted.

The lighting company, one of the world's three largest, saw net profit climb 17 percent to 262 million marks in the 1995-96 business year, which ended September 30. Sales rose five percent to 5.7 billion marks.
The company said sales should rise a "nominal three to four percent" in 1996-97. But profits would probably be unchanged as it reorganises its Sylvania unit in the U.S.
Declining prices throughout world markets, along with investments in Far East and Eastern European ventures, were also expected to hinder profit, Osram said.
The company said improved productivity would balance out the effects of increased investments and lower prices, resulting in level 1996-97 profit.
Osram has set out on a globalisation strategy in which it aims to draw 90 percent of its revenue from outside of Germany. Foreign markets now generate 86 percent of its sales.

Osram is counting on Asia and Eastern Euorpe to generate enough growth to increase sales a total of about 20 percent over the next three years. After a flat 1996-97, profit should grow at the same rate as sales, Osram said.
In August, the company formed a unit in Bucharest in Rumania to drive sales of energy-saving lighting products in Eastern Europe.
In the 1995-96 business year, which ended September 30, Osram's pretax profit rose 8.5 percent to 340 million, while its worldwide payroll declined three percent to 26,158. ($1=1.5647 Mark)
